Our method is a desk review: no funded account, no trades. We read the published material in full, including unfilled placeholders and contradictions, and scored five fixed dimensions.
whatItClaims: Signals generated without manual chart reading.
A US$250 minimum deposit to start.
Free registration, with account activation by confirmation link.
Risk settings adjustable before the first live trade.
A partner broker holding funds and executing orders.
whatWeChecked: The number reuse: one score figure doing more than one job.
The deposit terms: minimum amount, payment methods and where the money sits.
The demo claim: practice account confirmed in the signup flow.
The payout promise: within-a-day wording without processing detail.
The broker relationship: which partner desk executes orders.
The asset list: how many pairs are actually offered.

steps.title: Register
steps.text: Fill in the registration form and activate the account via the confirmation email.

steps.title: Fund
steps.text: Make the US$250 first deposit using any of the listed payment methods.

steps.title: Configure
steps.text: Set your limits, pick a trading mode and let the demo build your confidence first.

pros: Fast setup - minutes to a live dashboard.
Free registration and a demo account.
cons: Marketing numbers that the fine print walks back.
No independent audit of the models.
redFlags: Payout promises with no processing detail.
No regulator, licence or audit named anywhere.
Marketing numbers the fine print quietly qualifies.

faqs.a: 11 crypto assets through broker partners, per the published pages. The list varies between sections, so check the dashboard after signup.
Yes - the platform offers automatic and manual modes, so you can follow the signals or confirm each entry yourself.
US$250, funded by bank card, bank transfer, PayPal or Skrill. It is trading capital in your balance, not a fee - and it is exposed to market risk once live.

faqs.q: Does it offer a demo account?
faqs.a: Yes - a practice account is part of the package and runs alongside the live balance, which is the sensible first step before risking the US$250 minimum.

faqs.q: What does the published score actually mean?
faqs.a: It does double duty - a platform score and an early community response - and neither is independently verified. Treat both as marketing until proven otherwise.

bottomLine: The service behind the marketing looks functional, and a careful user can use it without stepping on the fine print.
We scored Vastofondizia AI 4.5 out of 5. The deductions come from the disclosure gaps, not the mechanics. With the US$250 minimum and the demo as guardrails, the risk stays yours to control.
